calls.role: You are the evidence synthesis agent.

You are an independent neonatal safety auditor. Check patient age/gestation, trends, renal impairment, allergy, danger signs, missing data, and unsafe reassurance or discontinuation. Guidance is not an automatic treatment order.
You are an independent source-entailment auditor. Check citation scope, exact evidence support, negation, contradictions and source applicability.

packet.evaluation_question: Explain whether a falling C-reactive protein alone excludes infection or permits stopping antibiotics.

evidence.text: Do not use C-reactive protein results alone to make decisions about starting, continuing or stopping antibiotics. [2026]

Measure baseline C-reactive protein concentration when starting antibiotic treatment in babies who may have neonatal infection. Use this together with any subsequent readings to assess the likelihood of infection and response to treatment. [2021]

If continuing antibiotics for longer than 48 hours for suspected late‑onset neonatal infection despite negative blood culture, review the baby at least once every 24 hours. At each review, decide whether to stop antibiotics, taking account of: • the level of initial clinical suspicion of infection and • the baby's clinical progress and current condition and • the levels and trends of C-reactive protein. [2021]

When continuing intravenous antibiotics for longer than 36 hours despite negative blood cultures, review the need for ongoing antibiotics at least once every 24 hours, taking account of: • the level of initial clinical suspicion of infection and • the baby's clinical progress and current condition and • the levels and trends of C-reactive protein concentration. [2012] 1.22 Switching to oral antibiotics

claims.text: A decreasing C‑reactive protein (CRP) value by itself cannot be used to rule out neonatal infection or to decide on stopping antibiotics.

support.quote: Do not use C-reactive protein results alone to make decisions about starting, continuing or stopping antibiotics.
Use this together with any subsequent readings to assess the likelihood of infection and response to treatment.

claims.text: Obtain a baseline CRP when antibiotics are started and repeat the measurement at 24‑hour intervals to evaluate trends alongside clinical signs.

support.quote: Measure baseline C-reactive protein concentration when starting antibiotic treatment in babies who may have neonatal infection.
Use this together with any subsequent readings to assess the likelihood of infection and response to treatment.

claims.text: If antibiotics have been given for >36 hours with negative cultures, review the need for continuation at least daily, considering initial suspicion, clinical progress, and CRP trends.

support.quote: When continuing intravenous antibiotics for longer than 36 hours despite negative blood cultures, review the need for ongoing antibiotics at least once every 24 hours, taking account of:
the level of initial clinical suspicion of infection and
the baby's clinical progress and current condition and
the levels and trends of C-reactive protein concentration.

claims.text: Escalate care (e.g., broaden antimicrobial coverage or seek senior review) if CRP rises or fails to fall while the infant shows worsening respiratory rate, oxygen requirement, or other sepsis indicators.
